title: Riverdale Pre-school
transcript:
Speaker 1: Sally: Good morning, Riverdale Preschool. Sally speaking.
Speaker 2: Robert: Hello. My name’s Robert. I’ve got a four year old daughter called Susie, and I’d like to get some information about your preschool, please.
Speaker 1: Sally: Sure, Robert. Well, Susie’s the right age. We take three and four year olds in classes of 20 students.
Speaker 2: Robert: Oh, great. And how many teachers do you have?
Speaker 1: Sally: We have two. The first group is taught by missus Oliver, and the second group is taken by missus Keogh.
Speaker 2: Just a moment. I’ll write that down. Robert: Could you spell the last name, please? It’s an unusual one, isn’t it?
Speaker 1: Sally: Yes. It’s k e o g h. Okay.
Speaker 2: Robert: I’ve got that. Now I know the children attend for two or three days a week.
Speaker 1: Sally: That’s right. The older ones, like Susie, are here for three days, which means fifteen hours a week. The younger ones, the three year olds, attend two days a week. That’s a total of ten hours.
Speaker 2: Robert: And what do they do during that time?
Speaker 1: Sally: Well, half the day is spent outside, and the children can run around and play games with their friends, or do a calmer activity, like painting, for example. We have a great outside play area that we’re improving all the time.
Speaker 2: Robert: Yes. We were walking past the other day, and Susie noticed. You’ve recently put in a new slide, haven’t you?
Speaker 1: Sally: Yes. We’re really pleased with it. It’s a big one, and the children love it.
Speaker 2: Robert: And are you thinking of adding anything else outdoors?
Speaker 1: Sally: Well, we were hoping to build a playhouse, but that was too expensive. So we’re now making plans for a garden where the children will be able to grow flowers and vegetables.
Speaker 2: Robert: Lovely. And what else do the children do?
Speaker 1: Sally: Well, the other half of the day is spent indoors. This year, the children seem to be very interested in music, so the teachers are doing a lot of activities related to that. Last year, there seemed to be more of an interest in dancing.
Speaker 2: Robert: Well, Susie would love either of those.
Speaker 1: Sally: The teachers may sometimes play quiet games with the children, but we always make time for a story each day. It’s a very important part of the program here.
Speaker 2: Robert: Yes. Of course. Robert: Now I’d like to ask you about the fees if that’s okay.
Speaker 1: Sally: Sure. We actually had to put them up this term, I’m afraid.
Speaker 2: Robert: Yes. I heard from a friend of mine that it used to be $420 for the term, but it’s just gone up to $470. Is that right?
Speaker 1: Sally: Yes. We had to add the extra $50 to cover costs. Things got a lot more expensive last year.
Speaker 2: Robert: I understand. And I think the fees are still quite reasonable. Another school I’ve spoken to charges $500 per term.
Speaker 1: Sally: Oh, really?
Speaker 2: Robert: My friend also told me that his daughter went on a trip to the local zoo and that the cost of that was covered in the fees. Is that right?
Speaker 1: Sally: Yes. We did that last year, but we’ll be going to a farm this year instead. We vary it. So, for example, we may go to the theatre next year.
Speaker 2: Robert: Okay. Sounds like fun.
Speaker 1: Sally: Also included in the price is membership of a special library. Children can borrow a toy and keep it for a week and choose a different one the following week. It’s very popular.
Speaker 2: Robert: What a great idea. We would certainly make use of that system if we enroll. Now is there anything else I should know?
Speaker 1: Sally: Well, the children have a rest here during the day, and we make up a little bed for them with sheets and blankets. But we advise parents to pack a pillow in the child’s bag as we don’t provide one.
Speaker 2: Robert: Okay. I’ll make a note of that. So what should I do if I want to come and look around the school during the day and meet the staff?
Speaker 1: Sally: The best thing is to call the teacher on the classroom mobile, and she’ll tell you which time is best to visit. Shall I give you the number?
Speaker 2: Robert: Yes, please.
Speaker 1: Sally: Okay. It’s o nine one four six three eight five two o.
Speaker 2: Robert: Thanks for all your help, Sally, and we hope to see you soon.
Speaker 1: Sally: No problem. Bye for now.
